text: Composting is an excellent method for enriching the soil and reducing chemical fertilizers. By turning organic waste into soil amendments, compost improves soil structure, richness, and aeration, leading to healthier plant growth and reduced reliance on synthetic chemical inputs. Composting reduces nitrate levels in water and soil, mitigating the risk of nitrate poisoning in children and the long-term impacts of exposure on ecosystems. Additionally, organic matter breaks down more slowly than synthetic fertilizers, prolonging the effective use of nutrients and minimizing leaching into groundwater. As urban areas increasingly adopt composting as a sustainable practice, the overall health and vitality of local soils are improving, complementing efforts to reduce chemical use in agriculture and landscaping. Moreover, compost can be used as a mulch or soil amendment in gardens and lawns, further enhancing soil quality and reducing chemical dependency.
